name: The Skeleton Courts
seat: the Drift Moot (an anchorage that moves; only the Storm-Bound claim to have charted it)
summary: The isles' answer to law: a confederacy of pirate crews, wreckers, and free harbors scattered across the Bone Archipelago's skeleton coasts. The Courts hold that no crown reaches past the horizon — and that what the sea takes, the sea pays for. They are the Storm-Bound's nemesis and, occasionally, their dance partners.

government.title: the Articles (signed by each crew)
government.current: no single head; the Drift Moot speaks when quorum anchors
government.note: Each crew signs its own Articles; the common law is the Wreck-Code: no drowning of sailors, shares witnessed, and parley held on neutral sand.

population.note: renegade hull-wrights; their ships don't sink
silence-sign spotters; the best reef-readers alive
exiles of the forbidden kind; unwelcome but feared

laws: The Wreck-Code: no drowning, witnessed shares, parley on neutral sand, and no working of the Glimmer at sea (the Veiled Sea's singing has made even pirates careful). Censer writ is mocked openly; seized Censer cargo is auctioned at the Drift Moot.

relations.note: They fight convoy actions by season and share rum by truce; each respects the other's dead.
Crown-chartered convoys pay the de facto 'horizon toll'.
Court crews have burned Censer barges rather than ransom them.

history_notes: Older than any living code-book claims; the isles' shrines predate the Compact.
Since the Veiled Sea began 'singing', three Court crews have sailed past the horizon deliberately. None returned. Two more are fitting out.
adventure_hooks: Players' ship is taken by the Courts; Wreck-Code parley gives them one night to prove worth better than hanging.
A Court crew offers players the Storm-Bound's secret chart of the Drift Moot — stolen, or planted?
The singing past the horizon has stopped. The Courts read it as an omen; the moot votes on sailing east in force.
